info.title: Turquoise Health Consumer Pricing API
info.description:
# Introduction

The Turquoise Consumer Pricing API offers an integration-ready solution to surface consumer-friendly healthcare service cost estimates in your application. By using our API, you will have access to cost estimates, including cash-pay and negotiated rates, for our full library of shoppable services for relevant provider and payer combinations.

Prospective integration partners can learn more about our underlying data and methodology below.

# Our Pricing Methodology

We leverage our  open license bundling methodology, Standard Service Packages (SSPs), and our rich healthcare pricing
database, Clear Rates, to generate consumer-facing cost estimates for most shoppable services and procedures.

## About our Standard Service Packages (SSPs)

Standard Service Packages (SSPs) are bundles of clinically related codes that represent what a patient actually gets
billed for a service. SSPs make healthcare costs comprehensive, accurate and relevant for patients.

We use historical claims to identify what most commonly gets billed alongside each primary procedure code, so each
bundle represents an 'expected' claim. All services, materials, and fees associated with a healthcare procedure are
consolidated into a single package including revenue codes, professional fees and ancillary services such as labs and drugs.

SSPs can be structured at three different levels of care: individual procedures or discrete clinical services ('items &
services'), single visit procedures ('encounters') or multi-visit care journeys for a specific condition ('episodes').

Most importantly, SSPs are consumer-first. They intuitively reflect the way a patient should expect to find, receive
and ultimately pay for care.

You can access our full, open-source library and read more about our methodology [here](https://open.forpatients.health/docs/getting-started/introduction/).

## How our Pricing Data is Sourced and Validated

Turquoise obtains pricing data from all relevant pricing signals, including payer and hospital Machine Readable Files
(MRFs), Medicare reference data, and historical medical claims.

Our pricing engine, Clear Rates, synthesizes all available sources, spanning reimbursement methodologies such as per diem
and case rates, to deliver a single, authoritative rate for every provider-payer-SSP combination.

Each price is derived by intelligently associating rates from our pricing engine into relevant SSPs. All prices surfaced
through our API have passed our verification process which requires each rate to be published by at least the provider
or the insurer, demonstrate low variability, and be corroborated by historical claims data.

The final result is a representative, consumer-friendly price that accounts for care delivery bundles, plausibility,
and even the nuances of upstream contract methodology.


# Data Coverage

Turquoise Health's Consumer Pricing API provides transparent, structured pricing data across
**over 13,000 providers**, **80+ payers**, and **200+ payer networks** nationwide. Coverage spans
all 50 states plus Washington, D.C.

## Provider Coverage

Our data includes price estimates for a diverse national network of providers.

| Provider Type | Coverage % |
|---|---|
| Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) | 37% |
| Short Term Acute Care Hospital | 26% |
| Imaging Center | 21% |
| Critical Access Hospital | 10% |
| Rehabilitation Hospital | 2% |
| Children's Hospital | 2% |
| Long Term Acute Care Hospital | 2% |

## Services (SSP) Coverage

The API sandbox currently offers consumer price estimates for **33 Standardized Service Packages (SSPs)**, spanning major
clinical categories including radiology (X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, mammography), surgical procedures (orthopedic,
gastrointestinal, obstetric, ENT), and diagnostic services. Our complete library contains over 150 SSPs, and is growing
rapidly. Read more about our SSPs [here](#api-1/description/about-our-standard-service-packages-ssps).

## Payer & Cash Pay Coverage

In addition to negotiated insurance rates across 80+ payers and 200+ payer networks, the API includes cash prices that have been
imputed from Hospital provided Machine Readable Files (network\_id = 0) for providers in all 51 jurisdictions.

# Getting Started

Our documentation site provides limited access to our Consumer Pricing API. If you require additional access to support
your use case, or if you are ready to integrate our service into your platform, please review the directions below.

## Authentication

The Turquoise Health API uses the **OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials** flow for authentication. This flow is
designed for server-to-server requests — your application authenticates as itself, not on behalf of a user.

### Obtaining Credentials

To get started, you'll need a `client_id`, `client_secret` and `organization_id`. To learn more, please contact our team
[here](https://turquoise.health/request-a-demo).

### Requesting an Access Token

Exchange your credentials for a short-lived access token by making the following request:
```bash
curl --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --request POST \
  --data '{"client_id":"<clientID>","client_secret":"<clientSecret>","grant_type":"client_credentials","organization_id":"<organizationID>"}' \
  https://api.turquoise.health/oauth/token
```

A successful response returns a JSON object:
```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGci...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600
}
```
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `access_token` | The token to include in API requests |
| `token_type` | Always `Bearer` |
| `expires_in` | Seconds until the token expires (e.g. `3600` = 1 hour) |

### Using your token

Include the access token in the `Authorization` header of every API request:

```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.turquoise.health/v2/example \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

### Token Expiration

Tokens expire after the number of seconds indicated by `expires_in`. When a token expires, your requests
will receive a `401 Unauthorized` response. At that point, repeat the token request above to obtain a
new one. We recommend proactively refreshing tokens before expiry rather than waiting for a 401.

get.description: List negotiated-rate networks, filterable by name (case-insensitive substring, matches network or payer name), payer_id (exact), relationships (provider_id/package_id — networks with at least one matching price), and one location mode: `location.near.*`, `location.within.*` (state/cbsa/zip_codes), or `location.zip`. Location scopes to networks with at least one price at an in-area provider, so `package_id` + location answers 'which networks price this package here' in one call. Results reflect networks Turquoise has priced. The network's payer is an {id, name} stub; the full entity lives at /v3/payers/{id}.
